Company Summary:

At Aliquantum International Inc also known as “AQI” the DNA of our company is based on integrity, social responsibility and commitment. This is a solid foundation for our passion to make life more comfortable with innovative functionality and outstanding design for all of our products. It is this corporate culture that forms a strong bond between our team all over the world. We feel continually challenged to inspire our customers and to offer only the very best products and services with innovative strength, teamwork, and premium brands. Our products are fun for all ages making them inspiring, engaging and collectable.

Job Description:

The National Amusement Deputy Director
is responsible for leading AQI's expansion into the amusement and redemption channel, the network of theme parks, family entertainment centers (FECs), and family resorts.  Primary focus for the National Amusement Deputy Director will be building AQI's account base in this channel from the ground up. This is a rare, built-for-growth opportunity: AQI already brings 20+ globally recognized character brands to the table, so the right candidate can hit the ground running rather than build a brand portfolio from scratch. While the title is Deputy Director, this role carries director-level accountability for forecasting, planning, account strategy, and P&L performance for the channel, with a clear path to grow into the Director title as the business scales. We're seeking an energetic, self-motivated individual with the ability to work in a fast-paced environment. The qualified candidate will have a bachelor’s degree and a minimum of 10 years of direct, hands-on selling and business development experience specifically within the amusement, redemption, and prize industry. Experience limited to general toy retail, adult collectible, or fandom/pop-culture consumer products does not satisfy this requirement. Candidates must bring an existing, active network of relationships across theme park, FEC, and family resort buyers and operators, ready to activate immediately upon hire.

The position will report directly to the Executive Director of Sales and will involve executing AQI's amusement channel plan to maximize overall corporate sales and profit goals. The Deputy Director will own the channel's P&L, annual budget, and multi-year account strategy, and will be held accountable for forecasting, planning, and financial accountability standards. This individual should show initiative and can develop sales programs for assigned accounts through creative and innovative planning. Travel is required both domestically and internationally for participation in trade meetings and industry relevant trade shows.

Specific Duties and Responsibilities:

·        Direct responsibility for identifying, cultivating, growing, and managing key accounts across theme parks, family entertainment centers (FECs), and family resorts in the amusement and redemption channel.
·        Create and implement short/medium/long-term channel strategies in conjunction with management and corporate objectives, executing the Scope, Pilot, and Scale phases of AQI's amusement channel plans.
·        Develop and coordinate promotional and co-marketing programs with key strategic amusement partners for new product launches and seasonal selling periods.
·        Identify buyer influences, redemption and prize trends, and product needs, converting them into AQI's owned and licensed brand categories.
·        Establish and maintain deep relationships at each key account, including buying, planning, operations, and management contacts.
·        Build and maintain the AQI Amusement Channel catalog in partnership with Merchandising, Product Development, and Design teams to ensure products are positioned correctly for redemption and prize formats.
·        Weekly account specific sales analytics and appropriate action plans, maximizing sales and minimizing risk, and building long term vendor and retailer relationships.
·        Forecast account product needs and achieve budgeted sales goals at established profit margins, reporting revenue against the channel's financial scenarios. Own full P&L accountability for the Amusement channel, including annual budget development, margin management, pricing strategy, and profitability reporting to the Executive Director of Sales and executive leadership.
·        Develop and present the channel's annual and multi-year account strategy, forecast, and business plan to executive leadership, including risk assessment and contingency planning.
·        Bring and immediately activate an existing network of senior-level relationships across theme park, FEC, family resort, and redemption/prize industry buyers and operators to accelerate account acquisition from day one.
·        Lead quarterly and annual business reviews with executive leadership on channel performance, account pipeline, and strategic initiatives.
·        Domestic and international travel is required for trade meetings and relevant trade shows.
·        Represent AQI at industry trade shows, including IAAPA Expo, Amusement Expo International, and NJAA.
·        Participate as requested in internal line reviews with Merchandising, Product Development, Licensing, and senior management.
·        Work collaboratively with other teams in the company as required.
·        Build, lead, and develop the Amusement channel team as it scales, including management of future hires and the hiring process.

Preferred Skills & Experience:

·        10+ years in amusement national account and business development sales; experience in the amusement, redemption, and licensed consumer products industry is an absolute must. General toy retail, adult collectible, or fandom/pop-culture consumer products experience does not meet this requirement and is not an acceptable substitute.
·        Direct experience with the amusement and redemption industry: crane and claw machine operators, FEC operators, or plush and prize suppliers.
·        Established, active relationships with theme park, FEC, and family resort buyers, procurement teams, and redemption/prize operators, sufficient to generate near-term account activity without a ramp-up period.
·        Prior experience owning P&L, budget, or account-strategy accountability at a senior individual-contributor or management level.
·        A hungry, motivated leader who wants to grow into a Director-level role as the channel and team scale.
·        Demonstrated ability to assimilate into a fast-paced, entrepreneurial culture.
·        Strong creative, communication, and interpersonal skills.
·        Strong analytical, conceptual, and problem-solving skills.
·        Skilled negotiator with experience owning pricing strategy, program terms, and co-marketing agreements with national accounts.
·        Comfortable representing a company at industry trade shows and building relationships with buyers and operators face to face.
·        Proactive, highly organized, with efficient time management skills.
·        Proficiency with MS Office Suite.
·        A proven track record delivering financial results.
·        Bachelor's Degree.

Apex Technical School, part of The Fedcap Group, is seeking a dynamic, energetic, and entrepreneurial leader to serve as Chief Operating Officer & Vice President, Administration. Reporting to the President, this executive will oversee the day-to-day operations of the institution while leading strategic initiatives that drive growth, operational excellence, student success, and organizational modernization.

The COO & Vice President, Administration provides executive leadership across institutional operations, including enrollment management, student services, workforce development, accreditation and regulatory compliance, instructional operations, technology, finance, facilities, and human resources. Accredited by the Accrediting Commission of Career Schools and Colleges (ACCSC) and licensed by the New York State Education Department, Apex is recognized as a 2024–2025 ACCSC School of Excellence and partners closely with employers and industry to ensure programs align with evolving workforce needs.

jobs.title: Chief Executive Officer
jobs.description:
For nearly 50 years, Project Return has helped the recently incarcerated return to community by connecting them to employment, housing, and the support needed to rebuild their lives.
Project Return has a staff of 17 and an annual operating budget of $3.7 million, supported by substantial funding from the State of Tennessee and the philanthropic community. The organization operates out of its own headquarters building in Nashville's Napier neighborhood and uses its real estate holdings to partner with aligned organizations serving the same community.

The Opportunity

Project Return was founded by a coalition of Nashville church leaders committed to grace, dignity, and second chances for people returning from incarceration. That mission connects returning community members to employment regardless of where their incarceration took place or the nature of their offense. This full inclusion remains a defining feature of the organization's identity, and a core value the next CEO is expected to protect and carry forward.
While the core mission of welcoming community members back to Nashville by providing substantive support has remained steady, Project Return has sought new ways to serve that mission. In 2013, the organization launched PROe, a social enterprise providing transitional employment directly to participants. Over the past decade, it has grown into one of the organization's most important assets: a primary reason people come through Project Return's doors, a proven training ground for real-world work experience, and a meaningful revenue driver.
Project Return has weathered a period of significant change, including leadership transition, financial restructuring, staff reductions, and a renewed focus on its core programs. The organization enters this search leaner and on stronger financial footing, while recognizing that important work remains to strengthen systems, clarify accountability, rebuild organizational capacity, and determine where future growth can be sustained. The next CEO will have the opportunity to lead Project Return from stabilization into its next era of disciplined, strategic growth.
Project Return seeks a Chief Executive Officer who is genuinely curious and energized by complex challenges. Project Return has a strong history of innovating its way forward, and the next CEO should carry forward that same instinct, looking for creative and sustainable ways to grow the organization's impact. The position focuses on executive leadership: setting direction, building strong systems, and holding senior directors accountable for excellent programs.
The next Chief Executive Officer will play a defining role in Project Return's next chapter. The most immediate priorities are financial and operational: building disciplined business and financial processes, growing the social enterprise into a stronger engine for both employment and revenue, and aligning the organizational structure to match its current scope of work.
Project Return needs a CEO who can bring discipline to the organization without losing sight of the people it serves. The CEO will need to strengthen finances and operations, grow PROe, strengthen processes and senior leadership, and represent Project Return effectively with government, philanthropy, employers, and the broader Nashville community.

Key Responsibilities

Strategic & Mission Leadership

• Clarify and build Project Return's strategic direction, using participant outcomes, staff experience, and financial realities to decide what to strengthen, what to change, and where to grow.
• Serve as Project Return's chief external ambassador and thought leader, strengthening partnerships with public agencies, elected officials, philanthropic partners, individual donors, and field-building networks to advance systems change and secure sustainable investment.
• Champion equity, dignity, and the right to a full and free life after incarceration, embedding trauma-informed and community-rooted approaches into organizational strategy, policy positions, and public engagement.
• Build alignment and shared purpose across Board, staff, and stakeholders, fostering clarity, trust, and collective ownership of Project Return's strategic direction.
Finance, Operations & Performance

• Provide fiduciary leadership for Project Return's operating budget, including financial controls, forecasting, and risk management.
• Partner with Project Return's contracted accounting firm to ensure accurate financial statements, strong internal controls, and reliable reporting.
• Establish an organizational and staffing structure aligned with Project Return's current scope of work, and ensure operations and infrastructure, finance, HR, IT, compliance, and facilities are integrated and appropriately scaled.
• Lead PROe as both a mission strategy and a business enterprise, strengthening its operating model, pricing, margins, employer pipeline, workforce capacity, and performance so that it produces strong participant outcomes while contributing meaningfully to organizational sustainability.
• Provide strategic oversight of Project Return's housing and real estate portfolio, ensuring sound property management, consistent policies and controls, regulatory compliance, financial sustainability, and alignment with the organization's broader mission and strategy.
• Integrate data, research, and lived organizational experience into organizational learning, using findings to refine practice and adapt to emerging needs and policy shifts.
• Use participant and program data to understand what is working, identify where programs need to improve, and clearly communicate Project Return's results to funders, partners, and the Board.
• Supervise, coach, and develop Project Return's senior directors, holding them accountable to clear goals while providing the support they need to lead their teams well; hire people for key leadership positions as organizational needs require.
Development, Fundraising & Communications

• Lead an integrated development and communications strategy and infrastructure.
• Serve as a primary steward of external relationships, cultivating and sustaining strong partnerships with public agencies as well as foundations, individual donors, and other key supporters.
• Partner with the Board to expand resources and visibility, activating board members as ambassadors, advocates, and connectors to philanthropic, civic, and policy networks.
• Diversify funding streams by building on Project Return's continued success securing state and federal grants and sustained foundation support, while exploring new opportunities for funding through the social enterprise, government contracts, and private giving.
Board Partnership & Governance

• Serve as the primary partner to the Board, fostering a strong, transparent, and trusting relationship, and providing timely, accurate information on organizational performance, risk, finances, and impact to support effective governance and decision-making.
• Collaborate with Board leadership on strategic planning, ensuring continuity, stability, and long-term organizational health following a period of significant change.
• Engage and activate board members as strategic assets, supporting their roles in fundraising, advocacy, and relationship-building, and partner with the Board on recruitment, development, and evaluation to build a diverse, skilled, mission-aligned Board that reflects the communities Project Return serves.
• Ensure strong governance practices and compliance, including adherence to bylaws, policies, ethical standards, and nonprofit best practices.

Qualifications & Experience

Skills & Experience

• A minimum of 7 years of senior leadership experience within a complex organization, whether nonprofit, public sector, or business, with responsibility spanning strategy, operations, finance, and external engagement.
• Experience strengthening organizational culture and accountability, including clarifying roles, addressing performance issues, navigating conflict, and creating an environment where staff can raise concerns while remaining accountable for results.
• Demonstrated experience managing complex organizations with multiple programs, revenue streams, or business lines, and a proven track record of financial stewardship, including oversight of multi-million-dollar budgets.
• Strong financial acumen, including experience with budgeting, financial oversight, interpreting financial statements, and partnering effectively with outside accounting or finance professionals.
• Experience leading organizations, teams, or divisions through periods of growth, change, or transition, with the judgment and steadiness to manage both opportunity and uncertainty.
• A demonstrated ability to operate at a strategic, executive level: setting direction, holding senior leaders accountable, and building strong systems, rather than managing day-to-day service delivery directly.
• Demonstrated ability to navigate conflict, difficult personnel dynamics, and high-stakes conversations with steadiness, sound judgment, and appropriate boundaries, while building systems and a culture that addresses issues before they escalate.
• Ability to build strong working relationships with government agencies, philanthropic partners, donors, policymakers, employers, and community organizations.
• A collaborative, values-driven leadership style, grounded in integrity and accountability, that builds trust across staff, Board, and community stakeholders.

Nonprofit Leadership LLC is facilitating this executive search on behalf of Project Return. Interested candidates should email a resume and cover letter to elle@nonprofit-leadership.com sharing an experience that shaped their belief in second chances and how it would inform their leadership. PRESIDENT & CEO

The El Paso Chamber of Commerce (the “Chamber”) in partnership with Sparrow Company, Excecutive Search & Staffing, is searching for an innovative, decisive, high-energy leader skilled at building relationships for the role of President and CEO. The ideal candidate will have the ability and vision to bring the organization forward and ensure the Chamber remains relevant in the changing environment.

POSITION SUMMARY:

The President & Chief Executive Officer (CEO) will provide high profile leadership, vision, guidance, and strategic direction for the programs and personnel of the El Paso Chamber of Commerce (the “Chamber”). The CEO will facilitate and lead staff and board efforts to achieve the mission and goals of the Chamber as approved by the Board of Directors. The CEO has full fiscal responsibility and oversight for all organizational operations. The CEO will demonstrate a working knowledge of economic development principles, the regional economy, political environment, marketing and branding concepts, membership sales, and the opportunities and challenges to support the growth and prosperity of large and small employers in the region, including a large military presence, healthcare, education, and workforce development. The CEO must possess the ability to embrace and inspire change and will demonstrate openness to ideas from a variety of sources and focus on achieving “best in class” outcomes.

ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES

Organizational Leadership and Management:

Working with the Board, the CEO must develop a shared vision for the future of the organization, build understanding around the mission, serve as an advocate to key stakeholders throughout the El Paso region and develop appropriate goals and strategies to advance that mission.

Responsible for all strategic planning and organizational policy as developed in concert with the board of directors which includes developing a long-term strategic plan and annual business plan with measurable objectives for delivery of successful outcomes on all Chamber events, projects, and programs; align objectives with annual budget revenue and expense projections.

Identify and create opportunities to grow the Chamber and support the business community through innovative ideas and practices, while continually evaluating programs and services to avoid duplication of programs and services that community partners are better equipped to provide.

Align and coordinate the Chamber with other economic development groups and like-minded organizations to develop programs and sponsorships that are mutually beneficial.

Provide oversight, support, and direction to ongoing programs at the Chamber.

Work with legislators, regulatory agencies, volunteers, and representatives of the not-for-profit sector to promote legislative and regulatory policies that encourage a vibrant community and address the issues of Chamber's constituencies.

Develop professional relationships and maintain effective contact with federal, state, and local officials as well as other business and community organizations pertinent to, or aligned with, Chamber projects or programs.

Financial Management:

Assume full financial oversight/accountability/responsibility to ensure the wise management of all Chamber resources.

Ensure the organization’s goals and strategic plan serve as the basis for sound financial management.

Oversee the fiscal activities of the organization including fundraising systems and programs, accounting, budgeting, reporting, and audit functions.

See that solid budgeting and accounting systems are in place and that appropriate financial controls and risk-management strategies protect organization’s assets.

Keep the Board fully informed of the Chamber’s financial condition.

Organization Development, Public Relations, Economic Development and Marketing:

Show Your Fire by joining our team and exhibiting your passion and pride in your work as part of our UNT System team.

Learn more about the UNT System and how we live our values at www.UNTSystem.edu.

Department Summary

UNT Health Clinical Practice Group is the academic clinical practice for UNT Health. Focused on improving health outcomes to build a healthier community. Clinical Practice Group primary and multispecialty care clinics are located on the UNT Health campus in Fort Worth. Our care teams extend to local hospitals, surgery centers, long-term and continuing care centers, and mobile and in-home care. The Clinical Practice Group’s interprofessional teams work collaboratively to achieve an optimized treatment plan tailored to the individual patient. Physicians, nurse practitioners, physician assistants, physical therapists, pharmacists, social workers, psychologists, specialized technicians, and nurses work together while intentionally integrating health care students, residents, and fellows to deliver care to our community.

Position Overview

The Executive Director provides leadership and oversight for revenue cycle operations, patient financial services, electronic health record operations, and related business applications. This position drives financial performance, reimbursement, regulatory compliance, technology optimization, and improvements in the patient financial experience. The role collaborates with clinical, operational, finance, compliance, and technology leaders to establish performance standards, lead process improvement initiatives, manage vendor relationships, and support the long-term goals of the Clinical Practice Group. This position serves as a member of the Clinical Practice Leadership Team and reports to the Senior Vice President/Chief Operating Officer.

Minimum Qualifications

Bachelor's degree in Business Administration or Public Administration and seven (7) years related experience; or any equivalent combination of education and experience.

Knowledge, Skills And Abilities

Knowledge of healthcare revenue cycle, reimbursement, billing compliance, and electronic health record systems.
Skill in strategic planning, financial and operational analysis, process improvement, and vendor management.
Strong leadership, communication, collaboration, and change-management skills.
Ability to interpret performance data, establish priorities, manage complex initiatives, and drive accountability and results.

Preferred Qualifications

Master's degree and/or professional certification such as CHFP, CRCR, or FHFMA. Equivalent combinations of education and relevant experience may be considered.

Job Duties

Provides executive leadership, direction, and oversight of revenue cycle operations through the Directors and Managers responsible for these functions, including charge capture, coding, claims submission, payment posting, denial management, accounts receivable, patient billing, collections, and resolution of patient balances. Collaborates with clinic operations and clinical leaders to improve front-end revenue cycle processes, including registration, eligibility verification, point-of-service collections, encounter closure, and other workflows that affect reimbursement and the patient financial experience.
Develops and executes a comprehensive revenue cycle and revenue integrity strategy aligned with organizational financial, clinical, access, compliance, and patient experience goals. Establishes long-range plans, operational priorities, and performance expectations that support sustainable net revenue, cash acceleration, regulatory compliance, and patient-centered financial services. Ensures accounts receivable and patient financial records are maintained confidentially and in accordance with applicable accounting, privacy, billing, and regulatory requirements.
Establishes and delegates implementation of goals, objectives, policies, procedures, workflows, internal controls, and systems for assigned revenue cycle functions within UNT Health Clinical Practice Group. Consults with Directors and Managers and evaluates departmental goals, performance trends, operational barriers, staffing needs, funding limitations, timelines, and resource allocation to accomplish organizational objectives.
Establishes, monitors, analyzes, and reports key revenue cycle performance indicators to assess operational effectiveness, identify trends, prioritize improvement opportunities, and support executive decision-making. Metrics may include, but are not limited to, eligibility verification, point-of-service collections, charge capture accuracy, coding quality, encounter closure timeliness, clean claim rate, denial rates, appeal outcomes, days in accounts receivable, net collection rate, net revenue realization, bad debt, write-offs, contractual adjustments, cost-to-collect, and patient billing performance. Works with clinic operations leaders to address front-end performance measures.

Leads denial prevention and management initiatives through root-cause analysis, payer trend monitoring, corrective action planning, and collaboration with operational, clinical, compliance, and finance leaders to reduce avoidable denials and improve reimbursement outcomes.

Partners with managed care, finance, legal, compliance, and operational leaders on third-party payer negotiations, reimbursement methodologies, contract implementation, and payer performance management. Coordinates payer contract provisions, reimbursement terms, and operational requirements with billing, collections, finance, and clinical operations. Partners with the teams responsible for credentialing, payer enrollment, and clinic operations to support timely provider enrollment, effective dates, and reimbursement readiness for new providers, services, and payer relationships.

jobs.description:
Position Summary

The Thurston Chamber of Commerce is seeking an accomplished, visionary, and values-driven executive to serve as its next President / Chief Executive Officer.

This is a rare and consequential leadership opportunity arising from the planned retirement of a long-tenured CEO who has guided the organization through decades of growth, program expansion, reputational excellence, and institutional development. The incoming CEO will be taking over an organization that is financially stable and structurally lean and nimble.

The CEO serves as the organization’s chief executive and administrative officer, accountable to the Board of Directors for all aspects of organizational performance, including strategic direction, operational and financial health, workforce leadership, and external affairs. The CEO is the primary face of the organization to the business community, elected officials, partner agencies, funders, media, and the public, and must be an effective communicator, a credible advocate, and a principled steward of the organization’s mission.

Essential Duties and Responsibilities

The CEO is responsible for the overall leadership, management, and direction of Thurston Chamber of Commerce. Essential duties include, but are not limited to, the following:

Strategic leadership:
Leads the development, implementation, and ongoing refinement of the organization’s multi-year strategic plan in partnership with the Board, executive team, and key stakeholders.  Identifies emerging trends, policy shifts, and community needs that may impact the organization’s direction, and proactively adapt organizational strategy in response.

Operational & Financial Oversight:
Providing executive oversight of all organizational operations, ensuring efficient, effective, and compliant delivery of programs and administrative functions across all departments. Directing the development and administration of the annual operating budget. Overseeing financial planning, audit processes, internal controls, and risk management to maintain the long-term fiscal health and operational sustainability of the organization. Serves as corporate secretary for two tax-exempt 501(c)3 and 501(c)6 organizations. Ensuring compliance with all applicable federal, state, and local laws, regulations, and funder requirements governing the organization’s programs, operations, and employment practices.

Community and External Affairs:
Serves as the primary spokesperson and public representative of the Thurston Chamber of Commerce to build and sustain relationships with chamber members, community leaders, and regional coalitions that help advance the organization’s interests and amplify its impact.  Leads government relations and advocacy efforts with policymakers at the local, state, tribal, and federal levels.

Workforce & Organizational Culture:
Leads, develops, and inspires a diverse team, fostering a culture of accountability, collaboration, professional excellence, and safety. Oversee the organization’s human resources strategy, including talent acquisition, employee development, performance management, succession planning, and total compensation philosophy.  Navigates organizational change thoughtfully and inclusively, communicating transparently with staff and maintaining morale and trust during transitions.

Board Relations & Governances:
Serves as the primary staff liaison to the Board of Directors, providing timely, accurate, and candid information and reports to support and inform the Board’s deliberation, decision-making, and fulfilling its fiduciary responsibilities. Supports Board development, onboarding, committee functions, and governance best practices in partnership with the Board’s Executive Committee.

Minimum Qualifications

The following qualifications are required for consideration for this position. Candidates who do not meet minimum qualifications will not be considered.

Education Required:
Bachelor’s degree from an accredited institution in business administration, economics, finance, management, public administration, or a closely related field or five years of senior executive-level experience.

Experience We seek candidates with deep executive‑level leadership experience, a track record of delivering mission outcomes, and demonstrated success in revenue growth and fund development.

Candidates should have experience with public–private partnerships, member‑based organizations, entrepreneurial and/ or small business pursuits, and environments requiring financial discipline.  They will bring a proven record of moving organizational vision into execution, expanded organizational reach, and strengthened relationships across sectors.

Additional Required Qualifications Demonstrated Profit and Loss (P&L) management experience.
Demonstrated ability to manage, build, sustain, and inspire a diverse and high-functioning team(s).
Seasoned and balanced understanding of regional, state, or local business environments. 

Other Preferred Qualifications The following qualifications are not required but will strengthen a candidate’s application and are weighted favorably in the selection process.
Experience working or residing in the Pacific Northwest region, with knowledge of Washington State’s governmental, policy, and community landscape.
Established relationships with leaders from private, public, non-profit, education sectors and with State economic development organizations.
Experience in fund development, grant acquisition, earned revenue diversification strategies that are subject to public accountability and transparency requirements.
Established relationships with federal or state agencies, legislative offices, regional or local regulatory, funding, planning entities / jurisdictions that are relevant to the organization’s work.

Physical Requirements & Working Conditions

This position operates in a professional office environment, with frequent travel in Thurston County and occasional travel throughout western Washington.

The CEO is expected to attend reoccurring and special Chamber events, community events, partner meetings, legislative meetings and receptions, and public forums, some of which may occur in the evenings or on weekends. Occasional out-of-state travel for conferences, federal agency meetings, or professional development is also expected, typically not exceeding two to four trips per year.

Ability to communicate effectively in person, in writing, by telephone, and via video conferencing platforms.
Ability to speak in public to small and large audiences, comfort with making video recordings and the use of a handheld microphone.    
Ability to operate a motor vehicle and maintain a valid driver’s license for regional travel purposes.
Ability to occasionally lift and carry materials or equipment up to 25 pounds.
Ability to navigate office buildings, community venues, and field sites, which may include stairs or uneven terrain.

Responsible for ensuring that all program-related paperwork is current, accurate, and submitted in a timely fashion.

Leads recruitment and retention of children enrolled in programs.

Proactively identify opportunities to enhance employee development and staff retention.
Participates in the development and delivery of staff training, including classroom and virtual presentations.

Complete other duties as assigned.

3 years minimum of Professional childcare experience, including experience supervising others.

For nearly 50 years, Project Return has helped the recently incarcerated return to community by connecting them to employment, housing, and the support needed to rebuild their lives.
Project Return has a staff of 17 and an annual operating budget of $3.7 million, supported by substantial funding from the State of Tennessee and the philanthropic community. The organization operates out of its own headquarters building in Nashville's Napier neighborhood and uses its real estate holdings to partner with aligned organizations serving the same community.

The Opportunity

Project Return was founded by a coalition of Nashville church leaders committed to grace, dignity, and second chances for people returning from incarceration. That mission connects returning community members to employment regardless of where their incarceration took place or the nature of their offense. This full inclusion remains a defining feature of the organization's identity, and a core value the next CEO is expected to protect and carry forward.
While the core mission of welcoming community members back to Nashville by providing substantive support has remained steady, Project Return has sought new ways to serve that mission. In 2013, the organization launched PROe, a social enterprise providing transitional employment directly to participants. Over the past decade, it has grown into one of the organization's most important assets: a primary reason people come through Project Return's doors, a proven training ground for real-world work experience, and a meaningful revenue driver.
Project Return has weathered a period of significant change, including leadership transition, financial restructuring, staff reductions, and a renewed focus on its core programs. The organization enters this search leaner and on stronger financial footing, while recognizing that important work remains to strengthen systems, clarify accountability, rebuild organizational capacity, and determine where future growth can be sustained. The next CEO will have the opportunity to lead Project Return from stabilization into its next era of disciplined, strategic growth.
Project Return seeks a Chief Executive Officer who is genuinely curious and energized by complex challenges. Project Return has a strong history of innovating its way forward, and the next CEO should carry forward that same instinct, looking for creative and sustainable ways to grow the organization's impact. The position focuses on executive leadership: setting direction, building strong systems, and holding senior directors accountable for excellent programs.
The next Chief Executive Officer will play a defining role in Project Return's next chapter. The most immediate priorities are financial and operational: building disciplined business and financial processes, growing the social enterprise into a stronger engine for both employment and revenue, and aligning the organizational structure to match its current scope of work.
Project Return needs a CEO who can bring discipline to the organization without losing sight of the people it serves. The CEO will need to strengthen finances and operations, grow PROe, strengthen processes and senior leadership, and represent Project Return effectively with government, philanthropy, employers, and the broader Nashville community.

Key Responsibilities

Strategic & Mission Leadership

• Clarify and build Project Return's strategic direction, using participant outcomes, staff experience, and financial realities to decide what to strengthen, what to change, and where to grow.
• Serve as Project Return's chief external ambassador and thought leader, strengthening partnerships with public agencies, elected officials, philanthropic partners, individual donors, and field-building networks to advance systems change and secure sustainable investment.
• Champion equity, dignity, and the right to a full and free life after incarceration, embedding trauma-informed and community-rooted approaches into organizational strategy, policy positions, and public engagement.
• Build alignment and shared purpose across Board, staff, and stakeholders, fostering clarity, trust, and collective ownership of Project Return's strategic direction.
Finance, Operations & Performance

• Provide fiduciary leadership for Project Return's operating budget, including financial controls, forecasting, and risk management.
• Partner with Project Return's contracted accounting firm to ensure accurate financial statements, strong internal controls, and reliable reporting.

PRESIDENT & CEO

The El Paso Chamber of Commerce (the “Chamber”) in partnership with Sparrow Company, Excecutive Search & Staffing, is searching for an innovative, decisive, high-energy leader skilled at building relationships for the role of President and CEO. The ideal candidate will have the ability and vision to bring the organization forward and ensure the Chamber remains relevant in the changing environment.

POSITION SUMMARY:

The President & Chief Executive Officer (CEO) will provide high profile leadership, vision, guidance, and strategic direction for the programs and personnel of the El Paso Chamber of Commerce (the “Chamber”). The CEO will facilitate and lead staff and board efforts to achieve the mission and goals of the Chamber as approved by the Board of Directors. The CEO has full fiscal responsibility and oversight for all organizational operations. The CEO will demonstrate a working knowledge of economic development principles, the regional economy, political environment, marketing and branding concepts, membership sales, and the opportunities and challenges to support the growth and prosperity of large and small employers in the region, including a large military presence, healthcare, education, and workforce development. The CEO must possess the ability to embrace and inspire change and will demonstrate openness to ideas from a variety of sources and focus on achieving “best in class” outcomes.

ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES

Organizational Leadership and Management:

Working with the Board, the CEO must develop a shared vision for the future of the organization, build understanding around the mission, serve as an advocate to key stakeholders throughout the El Paso region and develop appropriate goals and strategies to advance that mission.

Responsible for all strategic planning and organizational policy as developed in concert with the board of directors which includes developing a long-term strategic plan and annual business plan with measurable objectives for delivery of successful outcomes on all Chamber events, projects, and programs; align objectives with annual budget revenue and expense projections.

Identify and create opportunities to grow the Chamber and support the business community through innovative ideas and practices, while continually evaluating programs and services to avoid duplication of programs and services that community partners are better equipped to provide.

Align and coordinate the Chamber with other economic development groups and like-minded organizations to develop programs and sponsorships that are mutually beneficial.

Provide oversight, support, and direction to ongoing programs at the Chamber.

Work with legislators, regulatory agencies, volunteers, and representatives of the not-for-profit sector to promote legislative and regulatory policies that encourage a vibrant community and address the issues of Chamber's constituencies.

Develop professional relationships and maintain effective contact with federal, state, and local officials as well as other business and community organizations pertinent to, or aligned with, Chamber projects or programs.

Financial Management:

Assume full financial oversight/accountability/responsibility to ensure the wise management of all Chamber resources.

Ensure the organization’s goals and strategic plan serve as the basis for sound financial management.

Oversee the fiscal activities of the organization including fundraising systems and programs, accounting, budgeting, reporting, and audit functions.

See that solid budgeting and accounting systems are in place and that appropriate financial controls and risk-management strategies protect organization’s assets.

Keep the Board fully informed of the Chamber’s financial condition.

Organization Development, Public Relations, Economic Development and Marketing:

Facilitate the Chamber’s position as a leading representative of the business community in the Greater El Paso Area, advocating in a way that is respectful, shows integrity, and maintains credibility to the community at large.

Achieve and maintain high visibility in the community to create awareness and increase the perception of value of the programs and services and the political influence of the Chamber.

Officiate at public ceremonies, advise the public on complex issues, speak publicly, create a broad network of contacts, and represent the community in public forums.

Represent and promote the Chamber and its policies and objectives to a variety of audiences, including with federal, state, and local government elected leaders, the military community, collaborating organizations, and individual businesses.

Create messages that reflect the Chamber’s and its members’ position, relative to public policy, that effectively articulates the impact on the economy and/or the health and welfare of regional businesses.

Develop strategic direction and execute strategies related to marketing and communications to ensure that all Chamber members and the public are informed of the Chamber’s activities and achievements and role in the community.

Increase the exposure of the Chamber through the effective use of public media (e.g., Chamber publications and articles on Chamber issues, El Paso Times, El Paso, Inc.); develop ongoing relationships with target media, reporters, and editorial writers.

Oversee development of marketing messages, collateral materials, and website content through the optimal use of the Chamber’s digital capabilities to include an active presence via social media.

Optimize Chamber’s digital platform for improved member recruitment and retention by providing members and potential members greater and improved access to useful and relevant information.

Human Capital Management:

Oversee the management of Chamber staff including hiring, firing, performance reviews, salary and benefits administration, policy, and general supervision.

Coach and develop the internal leadership team to attain consistent, highly effective performance.

Develop and implement continuous improvement initiatives, better business practices and an organizational structure that will optimize performance and operating results.

Ongoing supervision of internal management system of key performance indicators (KPI’s) to monitor staff activity and performance against goals.

Promote a working environment of excellence, external and internal collaboration, and professional standards for the organization. Build accountability into the culture.

Board Relations:

Share the joint responsibility with the Board of Directors for developing and maintaining full transparency, a strong working relationship, and a system for sharing information that enables the Board to effectively carry out its governance role.

Communicate regularly to the Executive Committee and Board of Directors on Chamber programs and activities, political issues, and other issues relevant to the success of the Chamber.

Assist the Board in developing a long-range plan to build the appropriate Board to best represent the interests of the membership.This includes board succession planning, position development, and long-range candidate identification.

EDUCATION REQUIRED:

Bachelor’s degree; advanced degree preferred.

KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS, AND ABILITIES :

A minimum of 5 years of executive-level management experience which could include private industry, trade associations, economic development and/or related public sector or not-for-profit organizations. The ideal profile of career experiences would include a blend of the above-mentioned sectors including an executive-level role in the corporate or entrepreneurial environment.

A proven successful executive with a demonstrated record of delivering results in line with the objectives of the strategic plan and to provide dynamic internal and external leadership to the Chamber to achieve revenue objectives, budgeted annual gross and net revenue, and other program and financial goals within the annual business plan.
Knowledge and understanding of the business community, economic development, and political dynamics within the El Paso region and established relationships with the region’s influential leaders in business, non-profits, and politics.
Demonstrated ability to develop and execute strategic business or political strategies and manage the tactical execution to achieve results.
A business person with a record of accomplishment of involvement at the leadership level in community organizations, trade associations and public-sector organizations.
An excellent internal leader recognized for the ability to develop, motivate, and build functional teams that regularly achieve and maintain superior levels of performance.
Demonstrated ability to establish and maintain a credible reputation and high-profile presence in the community on behalf of an organization.
Proven excellence in written and oral communication and proven media experience are essential.
Experience in soliciting and securing sponsorship dollars from public and private sectors is highly preferred.
Proven experience in political affairs and experience of successfully influencing opinions of elected officials and in directing the focus of a community initiative or referendum campaign is highly preferred.

OTHER
:

Applicants with Certified Chamber Executive (CCE) credential, IOM or other industry recognized certifications or accreditations, may receive preferential consideration, but is not required.
Bilingual in Spanish/English preferred

Market-based salary and benefits package commensurate with the role.

MEDIA SCHOOL (BL-MSCH-IUBLA)

The Media School at Indiana University (IU) is built on a decades-long tradition of journalism, film, media, and communication at one of the nation's premier public universities. Our programs focus on teaching, researching, and creating media from academic, creative, and professional perspectives. The Media School is committed to building and supporting a strong community of students, scholars, practitioners, and staff.

This role, which reports to the senior director of development, offers an exciting opportunity to help shape the future of The Media School by strengthening connections with its global network of more than 25,000 alumni and supporters. A person in this role is a relationship builder who combines strategic thinking with hands-on execution.

Department-Specific Responsibilities

Leads annual giving and alumni engagement efforts, creating meaningful opportunities for alumni and donors to stay connected to the school while supporting scholarships, student experiences, faculty initiatives, and other strategic priorities.
Works closely with school leadership, the Indiana University Foundation, the IU Alumni Association, and communications partners, this position plays a visible and impactful role in advancing the school's mission.
Designs and implements fundraising campaigns, stewardship programs, and engagement initiatives that increases donor participation and strengthesn long-term support for The Media School. , the Associate Director will help
Grows a sustainable pipeline of philanthropic support while fostering a culture of lifelong alumni engagement and giving, using data, personalized outreach, volunteer engagement, and donor-centered communications .
Develops and manages donor stewardship activities, including personalized outreach, impact communications, and engagement experiences that strengthen donor relationships.
Meets with alumni and donors through on-campus meetings, virtual visits, and phone outreach to qualify prospects for annual and leadership annual giving opportunities and identifies pathways for increased philanthropic engagement.
Leads alumni engagement initiatives for The Media School's network of 25,000 plus alumni, with a focus on converting alumni involvement into sustained philanthropic support.
Designs, implements, and continuously improves The Media School's annual giving strategy in partnership with the IU Foundation
Develops engagement opportunities that connect alumni and donors with students, faculty, mentorship programs, volunteer leadership roles, and school priorities.
Manages the school's Distinguished Alumni Awards program, including nomination processes, selection coordination, recognition activities, and alumni relations opportunities.
Supports or implements development and alumni engagement events and initiatives across the school.
Serves as an ambassador for The Media School by communicating its mission, programs, accomplishments, and funding priorities to alumni, donors, students, faculty, and community stakeholders.

General Responsibilities

Identifies new prospects, cultivates relationships, and manages a portfolio and/or region of donors building a pipeline for solicitation.
Executes plans and designs campaigns to sustain and increase donations.
Collaborates with development colleagues' university-wide to align prospects/donors' interests with university funding needs and opportunities.
Maintains meaningful and consistent contact with potential donors to communicate university goals and solicit their support.
Introduces campus/school fundraisers to appropriate gift prospects for cultivation.
Documents communications, analyzes data, evaluates success and makes recommendations for change to campaign strategy.

Combinations of related education and experience may be considered. Education beyond the minimum required may be substituted for work experience. Work experience beyond the minimum required may be substituted for education.

Experience cultivating and stewarding donors and identifying opportunities for increased philanthropic support.

Demonstrates a high commitment to quality.

Highly thorough and dependable.
Demonstrates a high level of accuracy, even under pressure.
